author: ethan.brook News Editor
title: Downing Street Says Manchester City Is Not Above the Rules
text:
Downing Street clarified on Thursday that Manchester City is not above the rules after Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced criticism for remarks expressing concern over a potential club sale following a guilty verdict for financial breaches.
Downing Street Responds to Prime Minister Remarks
A spokesperson for Downing Street addressed the political friction on Thursday, stating that the initial judgment against the club is serious and that no one is above the rules.
Burnham credited the owners—led by Sheikh Mansour, a royal and the United Arab Emirates deputy prime minister who has backed the club since 2008—with playing a massive role in building modern Manchester and turning Manchester City into a global force. Speaking to the BBC, Burnham mentioned he was staying out of the matter directly, noting that the Premier League must handle it autonomously, and stressed that since Manchester City is disputing the claims, rushing to judgment would be a mistake.
“He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.”
No. 10 Downing Street spokesperson, via Yahoo and ESPN
Political Figures Criticize Comments
Shadow sports minister Louie French criticized the remarks, accusing Burnham of publicly backing the owners while the investigation continues and questioning whether political pressure is being applied. French called for the Government to keep politics out of football. Liberal Democrat MP Anna Sabine, the party’s spokesperson on sport, also weighed in, stating that fans of every club deserve to know the rules apply to everyone.
During his interview, Burnham maintained that he was not directly interfering and noted that the situation remains contested by Manchester City. He also drew parallels to how Everton, the club he supports, was charged with a more minor breach of Premier League financial rules in 2023, stating that he holds the view very firmly that the Toffees were not fairly treated in that process and that more people would say that wasn’t fair with hindsight.
Independent Commission Rules on Charges
The controversy unfolds against the backdrop of an independent commission’s findings, which concluded that Manchester City systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. The panel found City guilty of most of the 115 charges they faced, identifying a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m.
Manchester City has maintained its innocence of all accusations made.
Treasury Committee Questions HMRC
Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier has dispatched a letter to JP Marks, HMRC’s permanent secretary, inquiring if he knows about the panel’s conclusions—specifically regarding fake arrangements used to hide staff obligations—and whether he requested an unedited version of the ruling released on Tuesday.
A punishment hearing will be scheduled by the independent tribunal that convicted City, though setting it up might take several months, and the resulting penalties could involve a massive fine or a points deduction. Meanwhile, the chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), set up by the government in 2025, stated that the case had raised serious issues.
summary: Downing Street clarified on Thursday that Manchester City is not above the rules after Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced criticism for remarks expressing concern over a potential club sale following a guilty verdict for financial breaches. Speaking to the BBC, Burnham mentioned he was staying out of the matter directly, noting that the Premier League must handle it autonomously, and stressed that since Manchester City is disputing the claims, rushing to judgment would be a mistake.
